newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Million-dollar pigeon race set for Sun City.
newsitem.headline: Million-dollar pigeon race set for Sun City.

text.p: The homing pigeon will shake off its dowdy image this weekend in what organisers say is the world's first million-dollar pigeon race, from the desert of central South Africa to the glitzy casino resort of Sun City.
Some 800 of the best racing birds in the world are entered, at 1,000 dollars a head, for the 609 km World Free Flight race on Sunday.
Saudi Arabia's Prince Abdul Rahman al Faisal has 10 prize specimens competing in the event, a spokesman for the organisers said.
First through the timing trap at Sun City after a flight of around 10 hours will collect the first prize of $250,000.
Top flight pigeon fanciers from Belgium, Taiwan, the United States, and the United Kingdom brought their birds to South Africa a year in advance of the race to learn their new "home" destinations.

The first 200 pigeons through the lofts at Sun City will share the million-dollar total prize money -- organisers say that's the highest in the world for a pigeon race -- and top prices are expected when the winning birds are auctioned off at the end of the event.
